turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels, process/composition
    columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B, Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment
    step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2
    temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3
    temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3 cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2 temperature, Secondary treatment step 2
    time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3 time, Secondary treatment step 4
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure temperature, Thermal exposure time) and
    the two measured objectives `yield strength (MPa)` and `elongation (%)`
    (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose objectives were
    NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same process/composition
    columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH elongation (%). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), elongation (%)) plane, so a set of
mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates
that are all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis

**Approach:** Since objectives aren't given for the pool, I matched each candidate's composition + full processing route (HT/AH/aging schedule) against near-identical or very close entries in the training set to infer where each candidate is likely to sit on the strength–ductility trade-off curve.

**Key structure/property patterns found in training data:**

- **Semi-austenitic PH stainless (Fe~68-71%, Cr~18%, Ni~9-12%, Ti~0.3-0.4%, Si~0.4%)** solution-annealed with mild/no aging → moderate YS (~200-320 MPa) but very high elongation (50-70%). This is the ductile end of the frontier.
- **Ti-rich martensitic PH stainless (Fe~60-65%, Cr~11%, Ni~19-23%, Ti~2.9%)** with intermediate double-aging → YS in the 600-1000 MPa range with elongation ~20-30%, filling the mid-frontier.
- **PH13-8Mo type (Fe~75%, Cr~12.5%, Ni~8.5%, Al~0.95%, Cu~1.75%)** with low-temperature age-hardening (400-550 °C) → extreme YS (1200-1600+ MPa) but very low elongation (7-16%). This anchors the high-strength end.

**Matching pool candidates to these regimes:**

| Candidate | Closest training analog | Expected (YS, El) region |
|---|---|---|
| c002 | 68.2325/18/12/... HT1075+aging750/3000 → (245,58) | High ductility, moderate YS |
| c042 | 71.3625/18/8.75/... HT1150+aging600/10000 → (310,52) | High ductility, higher YS |
| c056 | Exact match to 60.4725/11.25/23/2.9Ti HT1120/4/120+AH735/16 → (620,27) | Mid YS, mid elongation |
| c012 | Same base comp, hotter HT/AH than (700,34) analog → est. (700-900, 20-30) | Higher YS, moderate elongation |
| c004 | PH13-8Mo family, low-temp AH250 (between 400→1287/10.8 and 450→1578/7.8) → est. (1200-1600, 8-16) | Extreme YS, low elongation |

These five span the frontier from very ductile/moderate-strength to extremely strong/low-ductility, giving good coverage for dominated hypervolume while remaining mutually non-dominated based on the training-data trends.

Final: c002, c042, c056, c012, c004
